Model
Mains
Eco
Most 230 V Pro-family machines sold in Europe and the UK have it: the machine turns itself off after 20 idle minutes and the power switch springs back when you let go.
Wiring
Stock wiring keeps the machine's harness and adds a few wires; Plug-and-Play wiring replaces it with the official harness.
Extras
Optional and unofficial: switch the machine on and off from your phone. Adds its wires, checks and steps to the pages. Drawn for Pro-family machines on Plug-and-Play wiring.

Eco-board machines need the power switch mod, and the official guide doesn't recommend stock wiring for them.

Gaggia Wiring

Every wire for your install, taken from the official schematic for your machine and voltage: where each one starts and ends, its color, length and connectors. Open the official schematic beside this page; it's the reference. This page draws it as a map you can tap through, then lists every wire to work down at the bench.

Sources

  • The official Gaggiuino stock wiring integration guide and its drawings (PCB v3.1/v4, redrawn in November 2026 with the mains wiring unchanged), read September and November 2026. The seven stock-integration wire names are the guide's; the LV run IDs are this site's.
  • The official Plug-and-Play/custom wiring guide, its four drawings and its two cut lists (GC_P v1.0), read November 2026. Connections, colors, lengths, connectors and the end labels (L1a, L1b and so on) are as drawn on them; each run's ID is its two end labels. BN2 is the cut list's neutral splice; BL, PL and PF (boiler lamp, power lamp, pump fuse) are this site's names for lead ends the cut list leaves unlabeled. The cut list gives G1d a 4.8 mm spade where the drawing labels the cup warmer's tab 6.3 mm. The site followed the May 2024 custom wiring until November 2026; that guide is now in the official archive.
  • Where a length isn't printed, the page says so. The stock wiring integration guide calls its lengths generous: route first, then trim. The Plug-and-Play cut list gives exact lengths.
  • The Shelly runs: fusio's "Gaggia Classic Pro + Shelly Plus 1PM Wiring" (220 to 240 V, PCB v3.1/v4.0), shared on the Gaggiuino Discord; unofficial. His drawing runs the machine's neutral through the Shelly's N terminals and feeds the power switch from the Shelly; Shelly's docs allow using its terminals as a bridge only at low currents, with the total under 15 A, and a 120 V Pro draws about 12 A on its own. So this site gives the Shelly its own neutral lead, keeps L1a-L1b on the socket, and joins its output to L4a's two wires with a splice. His drawing is on the May 2024 custom wiring; moving it onto the Plug-and-Play harness is this site's own work. The SH IDs are this site's.

AfterTroubleshooting

Mains voltage. This conversion puts your hands near 120/230 V wiring. Work only with the cord out, check everything with a meter before first power-on, and stop if anything here disagrees with the official Gaggiuino docs or your own reading of the machine. Nothing on this site has been reviewed by the Gaggiuino project. You are responsible for your own build.

Unofficial community material for the Gaggia Classic family. The install itself is the official guide at gaggiuino.github.io; these pages organize it, link to each step and add tools around it. Content is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, like the sister Silvia site. · Source and issues on GitHub
